memo.headline: Edge Compute behaves as a Voice AI component: standalone usage and demand fall well short of thresholds, so invest it as an attached capability.
memo.memo:
Behavioral: 66 accounts use Edge Compute (16.5% adoption). Only 8 are standalone and 54 are attached. Standalone usage share is 12.0% against an effective threshold of 35.0%, which was raised by 5 points because self-serve converts mainly with voice. Twelve-month retention is 40.0% for standalone (n=5) and 66.7% for attached (n=12). Both samples are small, so treat retention as directional. Gross margin is 55.0% for both groups.

Pipeline: 16 of 50 transcripts mention it, and only 3 frame it as standalone. That is 6.0% standalone demand against a 15.0% minimum. Standalone win rate is 0.0% on 3 closed deals, versus 83.3% when bundled. Losses cite latency, maturity and compliance. Competitors are Cloudflare Workers, AWS Lambda and Fastly.

Self-serve: the 90-day paid rate is 2.4% without voice and 19.4% with voice.

What would change the call: a standalone usage share near the threshold, or standalone wins in a larger deal sample. Next action: position Edge Compute inside Voice AI messaging and bundles, and address latency and maturity objections. This data is synthetic, so don't read it as real market fact.
